To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a type system should be designed to verify machine code; (2) the soundness proof of a type system should also be verified by the same type system; (3) the type checking of an input program and the soundness proof checking should be separated into two stages, the first of which can be efficiently interpreted by a logic programming engine; and (4) the logic programming engine should be able to handle both the type checking and the soundness checking

a type system should be designed to typecheck machine code, and the proof checking of an FPCC system should be factored to two stages: typechecking of machine code and verification soundness of type system.

(1) the design of interfaces for FPCC is a key issue; (2) a low level type system can be used to check machine code and the proof checking can efficiently be factored into typechecking and proof reconstruction; (3) the proof checking can further be optimized using a logic programming engine; (4) the proof reconstruction is a key issue in proof checking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a foundational proof carrying code system, and the design of interfaces among the three components of such a system.
the design of a type system and a proof checker for foundational PCC, and how to interface these components with a compiler and the safety proof to build an end-to-end system.
the design of interfaces and the implementation of the interfaces between compilers, type checkers, logic programming engines, proof checkers and the proofs of safety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a type system should be designed to verify machine code and proof checking should be factorized.
the design of interfaces is the key to building a complete end to end FP CC system.
we have built a prototype FPCC system, which is a complete end to end system including a type preserving compilation, a foundational proof checking engine, and a machine checkable sound proof.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of the interfaces between these three components is the key to building an end to end system.
we have built a prototype FPCC system that is the first end-to-end FPCC system, and the system is based on the simple foundations of mathematical logic.
the interfaces are the key for building a sound and efficient FPCC system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a type system can be designed to check safety of machine code and a logic programming engine can efficiently verify the correctness of a type system.
the proof checker should be a logic programming system.
a type system can be used to verify the soundness of the proof checker.
